artifacts.summary: Verification/inventory report: confirms session_liveness() ladder matches the task description's root-cause quote exactly at current HEAD, classifies all liveness_reason consumers as opaque interpolation (no literal-string branching risk), confirms cmd_session_list/cmd_session_reap wildcard defaults already preserve the required live:true/no-reap verdict for any new reason with zero code change needed there, finds a third undocumented 'five reasons' claim site (orchestrate-batch-admit.sh line 133) beyond the two named docs, identifies a test-coverage gap (neither named test file currently asserts the reason string for the below-floor dead-pid fixture), and documents the live suffixed-vs-bare session-id self-contention instance as orthogonal and out of scope.

memory_candidates.content: In agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/task-lock.sh, cmd_session_list's live_flag case and cmd_session_reap's reap-set case both key off `dead-pid|stale-heartbeat)` with a `*)` wildcard default. This means session_liveness() can grow new reason strings (beyond the five documented ones) without touching either consumer function -- a new reason automatically gets live:true (list) and is automatically excluded from reap (reap), by construction of the wildcard default. Only session_liveness()'s own ladder and its docstring need updating when adding a reason. session_contention()'s D4 liveness exclusion (file-scope-overlap.sh) likewise filters on the boolean `.live` field, not the reason string, so it's also insulated from new reason strings.

orchestrate-batch-admit.sh's --session-id flag must receive the SAME id string registered via task-lock.sh session-register, because session_contention()'s D4 self-exclusion compares them by exact string equality (.session_id != $own_sid). A per-task suffixed session_id (e.g. a bare batch id with a task-number suffix appended) passed as --session-id while the registry holds the bare id causes the self-exclusion to silently fail to match, and the session's own file_scope can contend against itself in later per-task dispatches within the same batch. Observed live in a multi-task /orchestrate run: registry entry used bare id, per-task delegation context carried the suffixed id.
